Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question:
1) Correct the sentence grammatically (Question no: 1-10)
She went to gym despite of her illness.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp:
Despite is the preposition. It does not take 'of' after it.
Therefore, the grammar mistake in the given sentence is 'of'.
Hence, the correct sentence is ''She went to gym despite her illness.''

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question: 2) Shreya, <u>who she is my best friend</u>, is a singer.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option1: ক) Shreya, she who is my best friend, is a singer.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option2: খ) Shreya, who is my best friend, is a singer
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option3: গ) Shreya, is my best friend, who she is a singer.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp:
The relative pronoun acts as the subject or object of the relative clause. It replaces words like she, he, him, her, they, them etc.
It is, therefore, wrong to repeat the pronoun in the relative clause.
Hence, the correct sentence is Shreya, who is my best friend, is a singer.

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question: 3) Can you tell me <u>why did you not speak</u> the truth?
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option1: ক) why did not you speak
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option2: খ) that why did you not speak
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option3: গ) why you did not speak
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option4: ঘ) why did you not spoke
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp:
This correction is related to the Embedded question. An embedded question is a question that is included inside another question or statement. such as: Do you know where he is?
In this type of question, the auxiliary verb, in the main question, generally appears after the subject.
Look at the example, it is not where is he? But where he is?
Go for details: https://continuingstudies.uvic.ca/elc/studyzone/410/grammar/410-embedded-questions

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question: 4) <u>Had I realized</u> how close I was to the edge of the valley, I would not have carried the bags there.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option2: খ) If I would have realized
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp:
When ‘had’ comes before the subject, it works as ‘if’.
Had + subject + v3 + other parts of subject, Subject + would have + v3.

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question: 5) No sooner <u>do the bells ring</u> than the curtain rose.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp:
No sooner is used to show that one thing happens immediately after another thing. It is often used with the past perfect, and usually followed by than:
No sooner + had + subject + Past participle + than + subject + v2.

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question: 6) Because of his ill health, the doctor has advised him <u>not to refrain from</u> smoking.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp:
Meaning of the sentence is not consistent. Since he is ill, Dr. advises him not to smoke.
refrain means to Stop oneself from doing something.
So, The correction will be omitting Not from the sentence.

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question: 7) Making friends is more rewarding than <u>to make enemies</u>.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp:
This sentence violates the rules of parallelism.
Parallelism in grammar is defined as two or more phrases or clauses in a sentence that have the same grammatical structure.
The sentence starts with ‘making friends’ so the correction will be making enemies.

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question: 8) Neither mr. Karim nor his friends <u>is invited to speak at the seminar</u>.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option1: ক) is invited to speak at the seminar.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option2: খ) are invited to speak at the seminar.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option3: গ) is speaking at the seminar.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option4: ঘ) are speaking on the seminar.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option5: ঙ) Will speak at the seminar.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp:
either---- or and neither ------ nor take verbs according to the nearer subject. In this correction, Verb follows his friends.
So, his friends are plural so the verb will be plural.

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question: 9) <u>Whatever he aspired to achieve, they</u> were hindered by his jealous step brothers.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option1: ক) Whatever he aspired to achieve, they
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option2: খ) Whatever he had any aspirations to, they
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option4: ঘ) Whatever be his aspiration, they
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp:
Dangling participles are not used here properly. Participles of verbs are often used to introduce subordinate clauses, which give extra information about the main part of a sentence (known as the main clause).
It’s important to use participles in subordinate clauses correctly. The participle should always describe an action performed by the subject of the main part of the sentence.
For example: Travelling to Finland, I found that the weather got colder and colder.
So, All the main clauses starting with ‘they’ are incorrect.

Go for details: https://www.lexico.com/grammar/dangling-participles

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question: 10) <u>Men’s interests in developing a cure for cancer have promoted</u> the rapid advances in the field of genetic engineering.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option1: ক) Men’s interests in developing a cure for cancer have promoted
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option2: খ) Men’s interests for developing a cure for cancer has promoted
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option3: গ) That men is interested in developing in developing a cure for cancer have promoted
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option4: ঘ) Interest in developing a cure for cancer have promoted
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option5: ঙ) Men’s interest in developing a cure for cancer has promoted
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp:
This correction has the subject verb agreement problem.
Interest is an uncountable noun so it is singular and it takes singular verbs.

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question:
11) Four parts of each sentence below are underlined and lettered. Identify if there is an error in any part; if there is no error then select option E. (question no 11-15)
We have no choice (A) but to appoint Maruf: he is the (B) best of the two candidates, and there (C) is no prospect of finding (D) more applicants.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp:
The Comparative Degree is used to compare two things to show which has the lesser or greater degree of the quality.
In the sentence, We are comparing two candidates, so we have to use better instead of best.

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question: 12) Either of the solutions you (A) <u>have</u> proposed (B) <u>are</u> acceptable to the union, (C) <u>whose</u> members (D) <u>are willing</u> to compromise.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp:
Treat ''either'' and ''neither'' as singular. Subject of the sentence is ‘either’ so verb is to be ‘is’ instead of ‘are’.
For details: https://www.grammar-monster.com/lessons/either_or_plural_or_singular_verb.htm

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question: 13) The reason I (A) <u>will</u> not be (B) <u>going</u> to USA this year is (C) <u>because</u> I will use up all my travel money (D) <u>attending</u> an important meeting in Singapore.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp:
This problem is related with redundancy. Redundancy refers to the repetition of the same idea or item of information within a phrase, clause, or sentence.
In this sentence, the reason and because are in similar meaning.

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question: 14) Employees with (A) <u>less</u> personal problems (B) <u>are</u> (C) <u>likely</u> to be (D) <u>more</u> productive.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp: Problem is a countable noun so It takes determinants ‘few’ instead of ‘less’.

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question: 15) By the time I (A) <u>phoned</u>, they (B) <u>had already</u> eaten breakfast and (C) <u>were</u> planning (D) <u>how to have spent</u> the holiday.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp: How to + V1 so it will be ‘How to spend’ not ‘how to have spent’.

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question:
16) Change the voice of the question no: 16 - 18.
Who is creating this mess?
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option1: ক) Who has been created this mess?
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option2: খ) By whom has this mess been created?
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option3: গ) By whom this mess is being created?
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option4: ঘ) By whom is this mess being created?
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp:
The question is in the present continuous tense. So, Passive voice structure will be:
By whom + am/is/are (changes with subject) + Object as subject + being + past participle?

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question: 17) Let me do this.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option2: খ) This is to be done by me.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option3: গ) Let this be done by me.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp:
Let this be done by me.
If a sentence is started with Let the passive voice of that sentence also be started with Let.
Rule :
Let + Subject + be + V3 + Other agents.

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question: 18) People speak English all over the world.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option1: ক) English is spoken all over the world.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option2: খ) English was spoken all over the world.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option3: গ) English was spoken by people.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.option4: ঘ) English is spoken by people.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp:
English is spoken all over the world.
Given sentence is in Present simple tense.
Rule :
Subject + (is /am /are) + V3 + Other agents.

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question: 19) Many times newspapers _____ the news to make it sensational
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp:
Distort means Give a misleading or false account or impression of.
Divulge means Make known.
Key Words: make it sensational. Newspapers do something that makes news sensational. So distort is the best choice. Newspapers divulge news but divulge of news does not always make news sensational.

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question: 20) Man who has committed such an _____ crime must get the most severe punishment.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp:
Severe means (of something bad or undesirable) very great; intense.
Abominable means Very bad; terrible.
Irreproachable means beyond criticism; faultless.
Key words: Severe punishment. Question of severe punishment comes when the crime is terrible. So the answer is abominable.

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question: 21) The judge used his _____ power and let him off with a reprimand.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp:
Reprimand means A formal expression of disapproval. Synonym: rebuke, reproof, admonishment, admonition, reproach, reproval, scolding, remonstration, upbraiding, castigation, lambasting, lecture, criticism, censure.
Residuary means Law Relating to the residue of an estate.
Discretionary means left to individual choice or judgment.
Key words: The judge has judgemental power so discretionary is the best choice.

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question: 22) Only those who have completed eighteen years are _____ to apply for this post.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp:
Legible means clear enough to read.
The sentence stated that a certain criteria is required to apply for the post. So ‘legible’ and ‘forced’ are inconsistent with the requirement. ‘Elected’ and ‘selected’ are not related to the application of this post. ‘Eligible’ meets the requirement.

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question: 23) The tyrant ____ anyone whom he regarded as a rival.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp:
Tyrant means a cruel and oppressive ruler.
Massacred and Slaughtered is used to mean the mass killing. A tyrant not always.
Exterminated means to destroy completely.
A cruel and oppressive person usually destroys his rival.

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question: 24) He sold his property because he was under a lot of__.
Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.exp:
Key words: sold property.
He sold his property due to owing money.

Sentence Corrections, Error Detection, V.question: 30) Only the fear of immediate _____ prevents that country from launching an attack.
